research_question: What is the effect of probiotics, compared with no active treatment, placebo, or usual care, on self-reported improvement in constipation (proportion of participants improved)?
control_label: Placebo, no active treatment, or usual care
outcome_description: Proportion of participants with self-reported improvement in constipation symptoms
positive_direction: A risk ratio greater than 1.0 (RR > 1) indicates a higher likelihood of self-reported improvement in constipation in the probiotics group compared to control.
search_queries: probiotic treatment functional constipation controlled comparison
inclusion_criteria: Empirical trials evaluating the effect of probiotics on constipation
Comparison of a probiotic intervention group to a placebo, no active treatment, or usual care control group
Reporting quantitative data on self-reported improvement or global symptom improvement in constipation
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentaries, and theoretical papers are excluded)

No comparison between a probiotic intervention and an inactive control condition (e.g., placebo, no active treatment, or usual care), or evaluating non-probiotic interventions (such as assessment-based nursing interventions)
No quantitative outcome data to calculate a risk ratio (missing event counts and sample sizes for self-reported improvement)
Completely unrelated to the treatment of constipation
moderators_to_extract: patient population (adults, pediatric, elderly, or functional constipation definition)
control condition type (placebo vs. usual care / no treatment)
effect_size_note: Binary outcome pooled as Risk Ratio (RR) using the number of participants reporting improvement in constipation out of the total randomized per arm.
